name: WITH
desc: Covers the WITH match expression: literal string/integer TEMP root names, sequential value-context bindings, lexical inheritance and restoration, unchanged NODE, inherited HAS/IS matching semantics, captures, transparent sequence/regex successors, namespaces, arbitrary names, and errors. WITH passes its final expression through in match context; it does not construct a value or support LOCAL-style computed names or null NODE overrides.

tests.name: Bindings and value types
tests.desc: WITH binds one or more literal TEMP root names and passes the final match result through. Value expressions accept all JSON types and are evaluated in the original current-node context plus earlier bindings.

tests.name: Binding values do not rebind NODE
Literal root names
tests.desc: Strings and integers are literal binding names. Integer names are coerced to strings; duplicate names overwrite locally. Dots and slashes are literal property characters and special object names must be safe.

tests.name: Root names do not expand paths
Sequential scope and restoration
tests.desc: Bindings are visible to later values and the final match, while each assigned value is evaluated before replacement. Nested scopes inherit unshadowed names and restore all bindings after true, false, or trapped errors.

tests.name: LOCAL in binding value does not leak
WITH final value function uses the local TEMP
Matching contexts
tests.desc: WITH preserves the caller matching mode and final expression context. Bare structures remain structural patterns, including embedded matches, rather than being evaluated into literal booleans. Explicit HAS/IS can override inherited mode. Bindings under alternate-target IS/HAS see that alternate NODE.

tests.name: Saved root fields remain accessible after descent
Alternate scalar target becomes binding NODE
Sequence and regex pass-through
tests.desc: WITH is a transparent match wrapper: sequence and regex terms retain every successor and their consumed width, including empty matches and multi-element terms. Bindings are evaluated where the wrapper starts; they do not advance the cursor. The scope ends before following terms.

tests.name: Following array term starts after wrapper
Binding reads the wrapper starting element
Following array term cannot see local TEMP
Regex bound from the starting codepoint
Regex can backtrack to a shorter successor
EXPR WITH remains a regex wrapper
Regex end can be a zero-width wrapped match
Regex following term sees the outer TEMP
Failed regex branch restores TEMP and position
Failed sequence branch restores TEMP and position
Captures and namespaces
tests.desc: WITH preserves captures produced by its final match and does not publish local TEMP bindings. Capture-suppressing wrappers retain their ordinary rules. CONST and STASH remain visible and unchanged.

tests.name: Date values remain usable in local TEMP
Failures and limits
tests.desc: Literal names must be strings or integers, so intrinsically invalid names and malformed arity are INVALID_GRAFT. Runtime binding/final-match errors are trapped as failed matches; syntax, resource, and unsupported-host failures remain fatal. Binding values are evaluated even if the final pattern does not use them.

tests.name: Missing binding value fails the match
Unused FAIL binding fails the match
Missing final TEMP fails the match
Binding allocation is fatal through NONE
